title: Gospel Foundations
tagline: Know and explain the core doctrines missionaries teach.
description: Learn the missionary purpose and the doctrines in the lessons of Preach My Gospel chapter 3: the Restoration, the plan of salvation, the gospel of Jesus Christ and lifelong discipleship. You will match key scriptures to doctrines and practise explaining each truth simply and kindly in your own words.

units.title: Your Missionary Purpose
units.description: Why missionaries serve, what the doctrine of Christ is, and how the Preach My Gospel lessons work.

levels.title: Why Missionaries Serve
levels.summary: The missionary purpose, becoming a missionary, and what success really means.

steps.title: Your purpose in one sentence
steps.body:
Chapter 1 of *Preach My Gospel* gives every missionary the same purpose:

> Invite others to come unto Christ by helping them receive the restored gospel through faith in Jesus Christ and His Atonement, repentance, baptism, receiving the gift of the Holy Ghost, and enduring to the end.

Finding, teaching, service, planning and even P-day chores all serve this one goal. When you feel unsure what to do next, ask: *does this help someone come unto Christ?*
steps.tip: Copy the missionary purpose from Preach My Gospel chapter 1 onto a card and keep it in your scriptures. Read it each morning until you can say it from memory.

steps.prompt: What is the heart of the missionary purpose?
options: Invite others to come unto Christ
Increase the number of Church members in an area
Teach people the history of the Church
Persuade people that other churches are wrong
feedback: Yes. Everything else in the purpose explains how: faith, repentance, baptism, the Holy Ghost and enduring.
Baptisms matter, but numbers are a result, not the purpose. The focus is people coming to Christ.
History supports the message, but the purpose centres on Jesus Christ.
Missionaries build on the truth people already have; they do not attack other faiths.
steps.explain: The purpose begins with “Invite others to come unto Christ.” The rest of the sentence describes the doctrine of Christ, the path by which people come to Him.

steps.title: Becoming before going
steps.body:
In 2005 Elder David A. Bednar taught: “The issue is not going on a mission; rather, the issue is becoming a missionary.”

Preparation is not a checklist you finish at 18. It is becoming someone who already lives what missionaries teach:
- praying and studying the scriptures every day
- repenting quickly and keeping covenants
- serving people and talking about the Savior naturally

Every one of those habits can start this week, at home.
steps.tip: Pick a set time for personal prayer and scripture study each day, like right after you wake up, and put it in your phone as a daily reminder.

steps.prompt: Elder Bednar taught that the real goal is receiving a mission call; becoming a missionary can wait until the MTC (missionary training center).
steps.explain: He taught the opposite: becoming a missionary (in desires, habits and testimony) matters more than the act of going, and it starts long before the call.

steps.title: What success really means
steps.body:
*Preach My Gospel* is clear that success is **not** measured by how many people you baptize or what leadership role you hold. People have agency; you cannot control their choices.

You are successful when you, for example:
- love people and want what is best for them
- live so you can have the Spirit and follow it
- work diligently and teach and invite clearly
- go about doing good and help build the Church

> Focus on what you control: your desire, your obedience, your effort.
steps.tip: At the end of each day, write one line in a journal: how you showed love, followed the Spirit, or worked hard. Focus on what you can control.

source.label: Preach My Gospel, ch. 1: A Successful Missionary

steps.prompt: Which of these are marks of a successful missionary according to Preach My Gospel? Select all that apply.
options: Loving people and desiring their good
Living worthy to have the Spirit and following it
Having more baptisms than other companionships
Working diligently every day
Being called as a zone leader
steps.explain: Success is about your desire, worthiness and effort. Baptism numbers and leadership callings are not the measure of a missionary’s worth or success.

steps.prompt: Two months into a new area you and your companion have taught many lessons, but no one has been baptized. Your companion sighs: “We’re failing.” What do you say?

options.text: “Let’s look at what we control: are we obeying, praying for the Spirit, working hard and inviting clearly? If yes, we’re succeeding. Let’s plan how to help the people we’re teaching take their next step.”
options.feedback: This matches the Preach My Gospel definition of success and turns discouragement into a plan.

options.text: “You’re right. Maybe we need to push people harder to set baptismal dates.”
options.feedback: Pressure ignores agency and usually drives people away. Invitations should be loving and led by the Spirit.

options.text: “Numbers don’t matter at all, so let’s not worry about goals.”
options.feedback: Success isn’t measured by numbers, but missionaries still set goals and plan diligently (PMG ch. 8).

options.text: “This area is just hard. Let’s wait for transfers.”
options.feedback: Giving up on an area means giving up on the people in it. Keep working and keep faith.

steps.explain: Missionaries measure themselves by desire, obedience and effort, then plan and work diligently. Results belong to the Lord and to people’s agency.

steps.title: You represent Jesus Christ
steps.body:
Missionaries must be called by proper authority. The call is generally extended by the President of the Church, and your stake president sets you apart. Your name tag carries the Savior’s name alongside your own.

That means you are not a salesperson. You are an authorized representative sharing what you know is true. A favourite missionary verse puts it this way:

> “O ye that embark in the service of God, see that ye serve him with all your heart, might, mind and strength” (D&C 4:2).
steps.tip: Memorize Doctrine and Covenants 4 one verse a day. In a week you will know the whole section by heart.

steps.prompt: Match each missionary scripture to what it teaches.
steps.hint: Two of these are in D&C 18. Think about which one talks about how much a soul is worth and which talks about joy.
pairs: Serve God with all your heart, might, mind and strength
God’s work and glory is our immortality and eternal life
The worth of souls is great in the sight of God
Great joy comes from bringing souls unto Christ
steps.explain: These four passages explain why missionaries serve: God loves His children, His whole work is their exaltation, and joining Him in that work brings joy.

steps.prompt: Write one habit you already have that is helping you “become a missionary,” and one habit you will start this week.

levels.title: The Doctrine of Christ
levels.summary: Faith, repentance, baptism, the Holy Ghost and enduring to the end.

steps.title: The Savior’s own summary
steps.body:
Nephi (2 Nephi 31) and the resurrected Savior (3 Nephi 11:31–41) both teach the **doctrine of Christ**, the path that leads back to God:
- faith in Jesus Christ
- repentance
- baptism by immersion
- receiving the gift of the Holy Ghost
- enduring to the end

It is not a checklist you do once. We keep returning to faith and repentance all our lives, and we renew our covenants each week through the sacrament.
steps.tip: Practice saying each of the five parts of the doctrine of Christ in one plain sentence, out loud, until you can do all five without notes.

steps.prompt: Put the doctrine of Christ in the order taught in 2 Nephi 31 and the fourth article of faith.
steps.hint: Think of the fourth article of faith. It lists the first four steps, and the last one lasts the rest of your life.
items: Faith in Jesus Christ
Repentance
Baptism by immersion
Receiving the gift of the Holy Ghost
Enduring to the end
steps.explain: Articles of Faith 1:4 lists the first principles and ordinances in this order, and 2 Nephi 31:20 adds pressing forward to the end.

steps.title: Faith: trust that acts
steps.body:
Alma teaches that faith is not “a perfect knowledge,” but hoping for things “which are not seen, which are true” (Alma 32:21). Faith in Jesus Christ is trusting Him enough to **do** what He asks.

A simple way to say it:
> “Faith is trusting Jesus Christ so much that you act on His words, even before you see every result.”

Faith grows the way a seed grows: you plant it by acting, then notice the good fruit (Alma 32:27–43).
steps.tip: Choose one small act of faith this week, like praying before a hard decision and then acting on what you feel. Write down what happened.

steps.prompt: A friend asks, “What do you mean by faith?” Which answer is most accurate and simple?
options: “Faith means being 100% sure without any questions.”
“Faith is trusting Jesus Christ enough to act on what He teaches, even before you see everything.”
“Faith is a good feeling you get at church.”
“Faith is believing that God exists.”
feedback: Alma 32:21 says faith is not a perfect knowledge. Questions can sit alongside faith.
Right. Faith is centred in Christ and leads to action.
Feelings can accompany faith, but faith is a principle of action and trust.
Belief is a start, but faith in Christ includes trusting Him and acting.
steps.explain: Faith in the gospel sense is centred in Jesus Christ and shows itself in action (James 2:17–18).

steps.title: The gate and the path
steps.body:
Nephi says repentance and baptism are the **gate**; after it comes the “strait and narrow path” (2 Nephi 31:17–18). Then:

> “Ye must press forward with a steadfastness in Christ, having a perfect brightness of hope, and a love of God and of all men” (2 Nephi 31:20).

Enduring to the end is not just waiting. It is pressing forward: feasting on the scriptures, praying, repenting, serving and keeping covenants for life.
steps.tip: During the sacrament each Sunday, think of one thing you will work on that week to press forward. Write it in your phone notes after the meeting.

steps.prompt: In the doctrine of Christ, “enduring to the end” mostly means waiting patiently after baptism.
steps.explain: 2 Nephi 31:20 describes active effort: pressing forward with steadfastness in Christ, feasting on His word, and continuing to repent and keep covenants.

steps.prompt: Match each part of the doctrine of Christ to a simple explanation you could use while teaching.
pairs: Trusting Jesus Christ enough to act on His words
Turning our hearts and lives toward God, with Christ’s help
A covenant with God, by immersion, by one with priesthood authority
The Spirit’s constant companionship, given by the laying on of hands
Continuing in faith, repentance and covenants all our lives
steps.explain: Being able to explain each principle in one plain sentence is a core missionary skill. Notice each explanation points back to Jesus Christ.

steps.prompt: A friend from school says: “I already believe in Jesus. Why would I need to be baptized?” What is the best response?

options.text: “Good question. Jesus Himself was baptized, even though He was sinless, to show us the way (2 Nephi 31:5–9). He taught that we must be ‘born of water and of the Spirit’ (John 3:5). Baptism is how we make a covenant to follow Him. Can I share what it meant to me?”
options.feedback: Respectful, scriptural, centred on Christ and personal. It invites further conversation.

options.text: “Belief isn’t enough. Without our baptism you can’t be saved.”
options.feedback: This sounds harsh and skips the reasons. Lead with the Savior’s example and teaching.

options.text: “It’s mostly a tradition for joining our church.”
options.feedback: Baptism is a sacred ordinance and covenant, not just a membership ritual.

options.text: “Don’t worry about it, believing is what matters most.”
options.feedback: This avoids the question and contradicts what Jesus taught in John 3:5.

steps.explain: Explain doctrine through the Savior’s example and words, then share personal testimony. This builds faith instead of arguments.

steps.title: Key takeaways
steps.body:
- The doctrine of Christ: faith, repentance, baptism, the gift of the Holy Ghost, enduring to the end.
- Faith is trust in Christ that leads to action.
- Repentance and baptism are the gate; the covenant path continues for life.
- Practise saying each principle in one plain sentence. You will use those sentences every day as a missionary.

levels.title: How the Lessons Work
levels.summary: The four lessons of Preach My Gospel chapter 3 and how to teach them flexibly.

steps.title: Chapter 3 at a glance
steps.body:
*Preach My Gospel* (2023) chapter 3 contains the doctrine missionaries teach:
- **The Invitation to Be Baptized and Confirmed**
- **Lesson 1:** The Message of the Restoration of the Gospel of Jesus Christ
- **Lesson 2:** Heavenly Father’s Plan of Salvation
- **Lesson 3:** The Gospel of Jesus Christ
- **Lesson 4:** Becoming Lifelong Disciples of Jesus Christ

In the 2023 edition, commandments, ordinances and the temple are taught inside Lesson 4.
steps.tip: Open Preach My Gospel in the Gospel Library app and read the doctrinal section of one lesson each week. Mark the key scriptures in your own copy.

steps.prompt: Match each lesson to its main focus.
pairs: God’s pattern of prophets, the Apostasy, Joseph Smith and the Book of Mormon
Premortal life, the Creation, the Fall, the Atonement and life after death
Faith, repentance, baptism, the Holy Ghost and enduring to the end
Covenants and commandments that help new members stay on the path
steps.explain: Lesson 1 is the Restoration, Lesson 2 the plan of salvation, Lesson 3 the doctrine of Christ, and Lesson 4 lifelong discipleship.

steps.title: A guide, not a script
steps.body:
Each lesson has a doctrinal foundation, key scriptures, questions and invitations, plus a short outline you can teach in about 3–10 minutes.

You are not meant to recite it. *Preach My Gospel* chapter 10 says to **let the Spirit guide the order of the lessons** and to adapt to each person’s needs, time and background.

That is why understanding the doctrine deeply (this course) matters more than memorizing wording.
steps.tip: Teach a family member a short version of a lesson in 3 to 10 minutes, in your own words and without reading. Ask them what was clear and what was not.

steps.prompt: Missionaries must teach the lessons in exact order and repeat the text word for word.
steps.explain: Preach My Gospel asks missionaries to master the doctrine and then teach in their own words, following the Spirit and adapting to people’s needs.

steps.title: Invitations are part of every lesson
steps.body:
Teaching without inviting is like describing food without offering any. Lessons 1–3 share common invitations:
- pray to know the message is true
- attend church this Sunday
- read the Book of Mormon and pray about it
- follow Jesus’s example and be baptized

Missionaries also usually agree on a time for the next visit. The invitation to be baptized and confirmed can come in any lesson, as you feel guided by the Spirit.
steps.tip: Practice inviting with a family member: ask a clear question that can be answered yes or no, like 'Will you read this chapter before we meet again?'

source.label: PMG ch. 3: The Invitation to Be Baptized

steps.prompt: Which of these are invitations listed in Lessons 1–3? Select all that apply.
options: Pray to know the message is true
Read the Book of Mormon
Attend church this Sunday
Donate to the missionary fund
Follow Jesus’s example and be baptized
steps.explain: Missionaries never ask people they teach for money. The invitations help people act in faith and receive their own witness.

steps.prompt: In a first visit, Ana says she felt peaceful while you talked about Jesus Christ. What is the best next step?

options.text: Ask what she felt, explain that peace like that is one way the Holy Ghost testifies, and invite her to follow Jesus’s example and be baptized, then keep learning together.
options.feedback: You help her recognize the Spirit and extend an inspired invitation while the feeling is fresh.

options.text: Move quickly to the next doctrine so you finish the whole lesson.
options.feedback: You miss a moment the Spirit prepared. Teaching is about people, not finishing material.

options.text: Tell her she must be baptized this week or she might lose the feeling.
options.feedback: Pressure and fear are not how the Lord invites. Invitations should be kind and clear.

options.text: Wait until the fourth lesson before mentioning baptism.
options.feedback: The invitation may come in any lesson when the Spirit guides; it doesn’t need to wait.

steps.explain: Help people recognize the Spirit, then invite them to act. Preach My Gospel says the baptismal invitation may happen during any lesson as the Spirit guides.

steps.prompt: Put this common flow for a teaching visit in a sensible order.
steps.hint: Think about what you need to know about a person before teaching, and what has to happen at the very end of every visit.
items: Build the relationship and learn about their needs
Begin with prayer to invite the Spirit
Teach a few doctrines simply, using scriptures
Share your testimony
Extend an invitation and promise blessings
Set a time for the next visit
steps.explain: This is a typical pattern, not a fixed rule. Understanding people first lets you choose which doctrine to teach; testimony and invitations come after the doctrine.

steps.title: Key takeaways
steps.body:
- Chapter 3 has four lessons plus the invitation to be baptized and confirmed.
- Lessons are guides: know the doctrine, then teach in your own words by the Spirit.
- Every lesson includes invitations; the baptismal invitation can come in any lesson.
- The rest of this course walks through each lesson’s doctrine.

units.title: The Message of the Restoration
units.description: Lesson 1: a loving Heavenly Father, prophets, the Apostasy, Joseph Smith and the Book of Mormon.

levels.title: Our Loving Heavenly Father
levels.summary: Who God is and why He calls prophets in every dispensation.

steps.title: Start with God’s love
steps.body:
Lesson 1 begins with the truth that makes everything else make sense: **God is our loving Heavenly Father.**
- He is “the Father of spirits” (Hebrews 12:9). Every person you meet is His child.
- He “so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son” (John 3:16).
- The Father and the Son have glorified bodies of flesh and bones; the Holy Ghost is a personage of spirit (D&C 130:22).

The Godhead are three separate beings, perfectly united in purpose.
steps.tip: Mark Hebrews 12:9, John 3:16 and Doctrine and Covenants 130:22 in your scriptures, and practice explaining the Godhead with them in under a minute.

steps.prompt: The Church teaches that the Father, the Son and the Holy Ghost are three separate beings, and that the Father and the Son have bodies of flesh and bones.
steps.explain: D&C 130:22 teaches this directly. The three are one in purpose, love and glory, but are distinct beings.

steps.title: A pattern of prophets
steps.body:
“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets” (Amos 3:7).

Across history you see a pattern called **dispensations**: God calls a prophet (Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses…), many follow, then over time people reject the prophets and truth and authority are lost. Then God calls a prophet again.

Jesus Christ organized His Church on “the foundation of the apostles and prophets” with Himself as “the chief corner stone” (Ephesians 2:19–20).
steps.tip: Draw the dispensation pattern as a circle on a card: prophet, people follow, people reject, truth lost, new prophet. Use it to explain the idea to a friend or sibling.

steps.prompt: Put the pattern of a dispensation in order.
steps.hint: The pattern is a cycle. It starts with a prophet and ends with a prophet.
items: God calls a prophet and reveals the gospel
Many people accept and follow the teachings
Over time people reject the prophets and change the teachings
Truth and priesthood authority are lost (apostasy)
God calls a new prophet to restore the truth
steps.explain: Recognizing this pattern prepares people to understand why a restoration was needed in the latter days.

steps.prompt: Match each Lesson 1 scripture to the doctrine it teaches.
pairs: God is the Father of our spirits
God loved the world so much He gave His Son
The Father and Son have bodies of flesh and bones
God reveals His will through prophets
Christ’s Church is built on apostles and prophets
steps.explain: These are key Lesson 1 and Doctrinal Mastery passages. Knowing where a doctrine is found lets you show people in their own scriptures.

steps.title: Say it simply
steps.body:
Try explaining the first two doctrines in under 30 seconds:

> “We believe God is your Heavenly Father. He knows you and loves you personally. Because He loves His children, He has always called prophets to teach them how to return to Him, like Noah, Abraham and Moses.”

Then ask a question that invites them in: *“How have you felt God’s love in your life?”*
steps.tip: Record yourself on your phone giving a 30-second explanation of God's love and prophets. Listen back, cut any words that are not needed, and record it again.

steps.prompt: Which question best opens a conversation about God at the start of Lesson 1?
options: “Do you believe in God?”
“What do you know about God’s plan for your life?”
“When have you felt that God knows you?”
“Did you know God has a body?”
feedback: A yes/no question often ends the conversation. Preach My Gospel warns against obvious yes/no questions.
Fair, but it assumes knowledge they may not have and can feel like a quiz.
An open, personal question invites them to share experiences and helps you understand their needs.
This jumps to a detail before building understanding and trust.
steps.explain: PMG chapter 10 encourages simple, open questions that help people share their feelings and experiences.

steps.prompt: A man named Daniel says: “I don’t think God cares about me. My life has been really hard.” What is the best response?

options.text: Listen and ask about his experiences, acknowledge that it has been hard, then gently share why you know God loves him, maybe Nephi’s words: “I know that he loveth his children; nevertheless, I do not know the meaning of all things” (1 Nephi 11:17).
options.feedback: You listen first, show empathy, and offer a true, honest witness without pretending to explain everything.

options.text: Explain that trials happen because of sin, so he should repent.
options.feedback: Many trials are not caused by personal sin. This would hurt and is not what the Church teaches.

options.text: Quickly move on to the Restoration so the lesson stays on track.
options.feedback: Ignoring his pain tells him you don’t care either.

options.text: Tell him everyone has hard lives and he just needs more faith.
options.feedback: True in a sense, but dismissive. Empathy comes before teaching.

steps.explain: Listen with genuine caring, respond with empathy, and then testify. People need to feel loved before they can believe God loves them.

steps.title: Key takeaways
steps.body:
- God is our loving Heavenly Father; the Godhead are three separate beings.
- God reveals truth through prophets in a repeating pattern of dispensations.
- Christ’s Church was built on apostles and prophets.
- Lead with God’s love, ask open questions, and listen before you teach.

levels.title: The Apostasy and the Restoration
levels.summary: Why a restoration was needed and how it happened through Joseph Smith.

steps.title: The falling away
steps.body:
After Jesus Christ’s Resurrection, His Apostles led the Church. Over time they were rejected and killed, and priesthood authority was taken from the earth. Teachings were changed. Paul foretold “a falling away” before the Second Coming (2 Thessalonians 2:1–3).

Teach this respectfully. Many sincere people kept the Bible and much truth alive, and other faiths contain much that is good. The restored gospel builds on that truth; it doesn’t mock it.
steps.tip: When you practice teaching the Apostasy, start by naming something good you respect in the other person's faith. Practice it with a family member playing the role.

steps.prompt: Teaching the Great Apostasy means telling people that their church is bad and has no truth.
steps.explain: The Apostasy is about the loss of priesthood authority and the fulness of the gospel, not about other people being bad. Missionaries honour the truth people already have and invite them to add to it.

steps.title: The First Vision
steps.body:
In 1820, 14-year-old Joseph Smith was confused by competing churches. He read James 1:5: “If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God.”

He prayed in a grove of trees near his home. God the Father and His Son Jesus Christ appeared. The Father pointed to the Son and said, “This is My Beloved Son. Hear Him!” (Joseph Smith—History 1:17). Joseph was told not to join any of the churches of that time.
steps.tip: Memorize Joseph Smith—History 1:16–17 word for word. Practice sharing it slowly and reverently, the way you would in a lesson.

steps.prompt: Which verse led Joseph Smith to pray in the grove?
options: John 3:16
James 1:5
Amos 3:7
Moroni 10:4
steps.explain: James 1:5 invites anyone who lacks wisdom to ask God. Joseph acted on it, and so can the people you teach.

steps.title: Authority and the Church restored
steps.body:
The Restoration continued step by step:
- **1823:** the angel Moroni tells Joseph about an ancient record.
- **May 1829:** John the Baptist restores the Aaronic Priesthood (D&C 13); Peter, James and John then restore the Melchizedek Priesthood.
- **August 1829:** printing of the Book of Mormon begins in Palmyra, New York.
- **6 April 1830:** the Church is organized.

The Lord called it “the only true and living church” (D&C 1:30). Revelation continues through living prophets today.

source.label: Printing and Publishing the Book of Mormon

steps.prompt: Put these events of the Restoration in order.
steps.hint: Use the years. When two events share a year, check the month.
items: First Vision (1820)
Moroni’s first visit to Joseph Smith (1823)
Aaronic Priesthood restored by John the Baptist (May 1829)
Printing of the Book of Mormon begins (August 1829)
Church organized (6 April 1830)
steps.explain: The Restoration was a process. Knowing the sequence helps you tell the story clearly.

steps.prompt: Match each scripture to what it teaches about the Restoration.
pairs: A falling away would come before the Second Coming
If you lack wisdom, ask God
The Father introduces His Beloved Son
The Aaronic Priesthood is restored with authority to baptize
The Lord calls His restored Church the only true and living church
steps.explain: Each of these is in Lesson 1 or in the Doctrinal Mastery list, so they are worth knowing by heart.

steps.prompt: Maria, a devout Catholic, asks: “My church has existed for 2,000 years. Why would God need to restore anything?” What is the best response?

options.text: Thank her for her faith and ask what it means to her. Then explain that Christ built His Church on apostles with authority (Ephesians 2:19–20; 4:11–14), that this authority was lost, and invite her to pray about Joseph Smith’s experience herself.
options.feedback: Respectful, scriptural and invites personal revelation instead of debate.

options.text: List the historical problems of her church to prove it went wrong.
options.feedback: Attacking her faith creates contention and drives away the Spirit.

options.text: Tell her it doesn’t matter and change the subject.
options.feedback: Her question is sincere and deserves a kind, clear answer.

options.text: Say that the age of a church means nothing and only revelation counts, so she should leave it.
options.feedback: Pushy and dismissive. Invite her to seek her own answer from God.

steps.explain: Honour what people already believe, teach the doctrine of authority with scriptures, and invite them to ask God. Conversion comes from the Holy Ghost, not from winning arguments.

steps.title: Key takeaways
steps.body:
- After the Apostles died, priesthood authority and the fulness of the gospel were lost.
- In 1820 God the Father and Jesus Christ appeared to Joseph Smith.
- Priesthood authority, the Book of Mormon and the Church were restored by 1830.
- Teach the Apostasy respectfully and invite people to pray about it themselves.

levels.title: The Book of Mormon and Prayer
levels.summary: Introduce the Book of Mormon and teach people to pray for their own answer.

steps.title: Another testament of Jesus Christ
steps.body:
The Book of Mormon is a record of God’s dealings with ancient peoples in the Americas, abridged by the prophet Mormon and translated by Joseph Smith “by the gift and power of God” (D&C 135:3).

Its title page says it was written for “the convincing of the Jew and Gentile that Jesus is the Christ.” It stands beside the Bible, not in place of it: Ezekiel saw two records becoming “one in thine hand” (Ezekiel 37:15–17).

If the Book of Mormon is true, Joseph Smith was a prophet and the Church is restored.
steps.tip: As you read the Book of Mormon, mark every verse that teaches about Jesus Christ in one color. It helps you find them fast when teaching.

source.label: PMG ch. 5: The Power of the Book of Mormon

steps.prompt: According to its title page, what is the main purpose of the Book of Mormon?
options: To record the history of ancient American nations
To replace the Bible
To convince Jew and Gentile that Jesus is the Christ
To explain Church policies
steps.explain: The history is real, but its purpose is to testify of Jesus Christ. That’s why missionaries call it “another testament of Jesus Christ.”

steps.title: Moroni’s promise
steps.body:
Moroni 10:3–5 gives a pattern anyone can follow:
- **read** these things
- **remember** how merciful the Lord has been
- **ponder** it in your heart
- **ask** God, the Eternal Father, in the name of Christ, if it is true
- ask with a sincere heart, with real intent, having faith in Christ

Then: “he will manifest the truth of it unto you, by the power of the Holy Ghost.”
steps.tip: Follow Moroni's promise yourself this week: set a time to read, ponder and ask in prayer. Write down any impressions right after.

steps.prompt: Put Moroni’s promise in the order he gives it.
steps.hint: Moroni starts with something you do with the book and ends with something you do in prayer.
items: Read the record
Remember the Lord’s mercy
Ponder it in your heart
Ask God in the name of Christ with real intent
Receive the answer by the power of the Holy Ghost
steps.explain: Moroni 10:3–5. Real intent means being willing to act on the answer.

steps.title: Teach people how to pray
steps.body:
Many people have never prayed out loud. Teach four simple parts:
1. Address **Heavenly Father**.
2. **Thank** Him for specific blessings.
3. **Ask** Him for what you need (including whether this message is true).
4. Close **in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.**

Then invite them to pray right there, or offer to pray first as an example. Speak reverently, but sincerity matters more than perfect wording.
steps.tip: Offer to say family prayer this week, and use the four simple parts out loud. It is good practice for teaching others how to pray.

steps.prompt: Put the parts of a prayer in order.
steps.hint: Think of how a letter is built: who it is to, what you want to say, and how you sign it.
items: “Dear Heavenly Father…”
“I thank Thee for…”
“I ask Thee…”
“In the name of Jesus Christ, amen.”
steps.explain: We pray to the Father, in the name of the Son (3 Nephi 18:19–21). This simple pattern works in any language.

steps.prompt: An answer from the Holy Ghost always comes as a powerful emotional experience, often with tears.
steps.explain: Preach My Gospel chapter 4 quotes President Howard W. Hunter cautioning against equating strong emotion or tears with the Spirit. The Spirit usually speaks quietly to the mind and heart (D&C 8:2–3), like the “still small voice” (1 Kings 19:12).

steps.prompt: Kevin says: “I read the chapter you gave me and prayed, but I didn’t feel anything.” What is the best response?

options.text: Thank him for trying, ask what he read and noticed, explain that the Spirit often speaks quietly as peace or good thoughts, share how you got your answer, and invite him to keep reading and praying.
options.feedback: Encouraging and honest. It helps him recognize quiet answers and keep acting in faith (Ether 12:6).

options.text: “You probably didn’t have real intent.”
options.feedback: This judges his heart and may discourage him.

options.text: “Then maybe this isn’t for you.”
options.feedback: Answers often come over time. Don’t give up on someone after one attempt.

options.text: Tell him that if he gets baptized, the feeling will come.
options.feedback: He needs his own witness first. Don’t skip the process of conversion.

steps.explain: “Ye receive no witness until after the trial of your faith” (Ether 12:6). Help people recognize quiet impressions and keep acting in faith.

steps.prompt: Write a 2–3 sentence introduction of the Book of Mormon you could give a friend, in your own words, including how it has blessed you.
steps.placeholder: The Book of Mormon is... For me, it has...

units.title: The Plan of Salvation
units.description: Lesson 2: where we came from, why we are here, and where we go after this life.

levels.title: Premortal Life, Creation and the Fall
levels.summary: Our life before birth, why the earth was created, and why the Fall was part of the plan.

steps.title: We lived before
steps.body:
Before birth we lived with Heavenly Father as His spirit children (Hebrews 12:9; Abraham 3:22–23). He presented a plan so we could become like Him: we would receive bodies, be tested, and use our **agency** (the power to choose).

Jesus Christ was chosen to be our Savior. God’s purpose is summed up in Moses 1:39:

> “This is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.”
steps.tip: Memorize Moses 1:39. Say it each night before bed for a week, and try to explain it to someone in your own words.

steps.prompt: Match each scripture to the doctrine it teaches.
pairs: Our spirits were organized before the world was
God’s work is our immortality and eternal life
God knew and ordained Jeremiah before he was born
We are created in the image of God
steps.explain: All four are Doctrinal Mastery passages that support the premortal part of the plan.

steps.title: The Creation
steps.body:
Under the Father’s direction, Jesus Christ created the earth (D&C 76:24; John 1:3). It was made so we could receive physical bodies and be tested.

Abraham 3:25 explains the test: “we will prove them herewith, to see if they will do all things whatsoever the Lord their God shall command them.”

A simple way to say it: *earth life is a school, not a punishment.*

steps.prompt: According to Abraham 3:25, why were we placed on earth?
options: To be punished for mistakes in the premortal life
To see if we will do all things God commands
To wait until the Second Coming
Because there was no room in heaven
steps.explain: Earth life is a time of testing and growth where we show what we will choose.

steps.title: The Fall: a necessary step
steps.body:
Adam and Eve chose to eat the fruit. As a result they left the garden, became mortal, could have children, and experienced opposition, sin, sickness and death.

Latter-day Saints see the Fall as part of God’s plan, not as ruining it:

> “Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy” (2 Nephi 2:25).

Eve rejoiced that without it they would never have known “the joy of our redemption” (Moses 5:11). And we are punished for our own sins, not for Adam’s transgression (Articles of Faith 1:2).
steps.tip: Read 2 Nephi 2 a few verses a day for a week, and write down one question each day to study or ask a parent or teacher about.

steps.prompt: Latter-day Saints believe the Fall of Adam and Eve was a tragic mistake that spoiled God’s plan.
steps.explain: 2 Nephi 2:25 and Moses 5:10–11 teach that the Fall made mortal life, families and progression possible. A Savior was prepared from the beginning to overcome its effects.

steps.prompt: Which of these were results of the Fall? Select all that apply.
options: Mortal bodies that would one day die
The ability to have children
Separation from God’s presence (spiritual death)
Every person is punished for Adam’s transgression
Experiencing opposition and learning good from evil
steps.explain: Articles of Faith 1:2: “men will be punished for their own sins, and not for Adam’s transgression.” The other four are real effects of the Fall that Jesus Christ helps us overcome.

steps.prompt: A classmate asks: “If God is loving, why did He let Adam and Eve fall and bring suffering into the world?” What is the best response?

options.text: Explain that the Fall let us be born, choose and grow, that opposition is needed to learn (2 Nephi 2:11, 25), and that God prepared a Savior from the beginning to heal what the Fall brought.
options.feedback: Clear, hopeful and doctrinally accurate.

options.text: “Nobody really knows; it’s a mystery.”
options.feedback: There are mysteries, but the restored gospel gives a clear, hopeful answer here.

options.text: “Eve messed everything up, so we all suffer.”
options.feedback: This contradicts the restored doctrine, which honours Eve’s choice (Moses 5:11).

options.text: “Suffering is punishment for Adam’s sin.”
options.feedback: Articles of Faith 1:2 rejects this.

steps.explain: The restored gospel uniquely shows the Fall as part of a loving plan, with Jesus Christ at its centre.

steps.title: Key takeaways
steps.body:
- We lived as God’s spirit children before birth and chose His plan.
- Jesus Christ created the earth as a place to gain bodies and be tested.
- The Fall brought mortality, families and opposition; it was a needed step.
- We answer for our own sins, not Adam’s.

levels.title: Life, the Atonement and the Spirit World
levels.summary: Why we are here, how Jesus Christ rescues us, and what happens at death.

steps.title: Why we are here
steps.body:
Mortal life lets us:
- gain a physical body
- learn by experience, including opposition (2 Nephi 2:11)
- use agency: we are “free to choose liberty and eternal life… or… captivity and death” (2 Nephi 2:27)
- make and keep covenants

Amulek said “this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God” (Alma 34:32).

steps.prompt: Which verse teaches that “this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God”?
options: Alma 34:32
2 Nephi 2:25
Moses 1:39
John 3:5
steps.explain: Alma 34:32 is a key verse for explaining the purpose of mortal life.

steps.title: The Atonement of Jesus Christ
steps.body:
In Gethsemane and on the cross, Jesus Christ suffered for our sins, and He also took upon Himself our “pains and afflictions and temptations of every kind” and our sicknesses, so He would know how to succor (help) us (Alma 7:11–13).

Then He rose from the dead. His Atonement overcomes:
- **physical death**: everyone will be resurrected (1 Corinthians 15:22)
- **spiritual death**: we can be forgiven and cleansed as we repent (D&C 19:16–19)
steps.tip: Read Alma 7:11–13, then write a few lines about one hard thing in your life the Savior understands. Pray about it that night.

steps.prompt: Match each scripture to what it teaches about the Savior’s Atonement.
pairs: He took on our pains and sicknesses to know how to help us
He suffered for all so they need not suffer if they repent
As in Adam all die, so in Christ all are made alive
He has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows
An infinite and eternal sacrifice was needed
steps.explain: All five are Doctrinal Mastery passages. The Atonement covers sin, pain, sorrow and death.

steps.prompt: Because of Jesus Christ, every person who has lived on earth will be resurrected.
steps.explain: Resurrection is a free gift to all (1 Corinthians 15:22; Alma 11:42–44). Forgiveness of sin and exaltation depend on repentance and covenants.

steps.title: The spirit world
steps.body:
At death, our spirit leaves the body and enters the spirit world. Alma describes **paradise**, “a state of rest” for the righteous, and a condition sometimes called spirit prison for those who did not receive or follow the truth (Alma 40:11–14).

God is just and merciful: the gospel is preached to the dead (1 Peter 4:6; D&C 138:32–34). In temples, members perform ordinances like baptism for those who have died, who can choose to accept them (1 Corinthians 15:29).
steps.tip: Ask your family or your ward temple and family history leader to help you find an ancestor on FamilySearch whose temple ordinances still need to be done.

steps.prompt: Which statements about the spirit world are taught in the scriptures? Select all that apply.
options: The righteous enter a state of rest called paradise
The gospel is preached to those who died without it
People who die without baptism lose all chance forever
Ordinances can be performed in temples for those who have died
Spirits in the spirit world no longer have agency
steps.explain: 1 Peter 4:6 and D&C 138 teach that the gospel is preached to the dead and they can choose to accept it. That requires agency.

steps.prompt: James tells you his mother died last year without ever hearing about Jesus Christ. He’s afraid she is lost forever. What do you say?

options.text: Express sympathy and let him talk about her. Then share that God has provided for everyone: the gospel is preached in the spirit world (1 Peter 4:6), and ordinances can be done for her in temples. Testify that God loves her.
options.feedback: Compassionate and full of the hope that the restored gospel uniquely offers.

options.text: Tell him that without baptism she can’t be saved.
options.feedback: Incomplete and hurtful. It leaves out God’s provision for the dead.

options.text: Avoid the topic because it might upset him.
options.feedback: He raised it. This doctrine could bring him real peace.

options.text: Promise that you know exactly where she is right now.
options.feedback: Don’t claim knowledge you don’t have. Teach the doctrine and let the Spirit comfort.

steps.explain: The plan of salvation answers the question “What happens to people who die without the gospel?” with hope: the Lord provides a way for all His children.

steps.title: Key takeaways
steps.body:
- We came to earth to gain a body, learn, choose and make covenants.
- Jesus Christ’s Atonement overcomes physical and spiritual death and heals our pain.
- After death we go to the spirit world, where the gospel is also taught.
- Temple ordinances for the dead show God’s fairness and love.

levels.title: Resurrection, Judgment and Glory
levels.summary: What resurrection is, how we are judged, and the kingdoms of glory.

steps.title: Resurrection
steps.body:
Resurrection is the reuniting of spirit and body in a perfect, immortal form that will never die again (Alma 11:43–45).

The resurrected Savior invited His disciples to touch Him: “a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have” (Luke 24:39). Because He rose, so will we.

steps.prompt: Luke 24:36–39 teaches that the resurrected Jesus was only a spirit.
steps.explain: Jesus said a spirit does not have flesh and bones “as ye see me have.” He had a resurrected, physical body.

steps.title: Judgment
steps.body:
After the Resurrection we will be judged by Jesus Christ according to our works (Revelation 20:12) and the desires of our hearts (D&C 137:9).

The Judge is also our Advocate. Those who repent are judged with mercy through His Atonement.

steps.title: Kingdoms of glory
steps.body:
Paul compared resurrected glories to the sun, moon and stars (1 Corinthians 15:40–42). D&C 76 explains:
- **Celestial:** those who receive the testimony of Jesus, are baptized and keep their covenants.
- **Terrestrial:** honourable people who were not valiant in the testimony of Jesus.
- **Telestial:** those who rejected the gospel and lived wickedly, after suffering for their own sins.

Even the telestial glory “surpasses all understanding” (D&C 76:89). The highest degree of the celestial kingdom requires the new and everlasting covenant of marriage (D&C 131:1–4).
steps.tip: Draw the plan of salvation on one sheet of paper from memory, then check it against Lesson 2 and fix anything you missed. Repeat until it is easy.

steps.prompt: Match each kingdom of glory to its description.
pairs: Glory like the sun; for those who receive the testimony of Jesus and keep covenants
Glory like the moon; honourable people not valiant in the testimony of Jesus
Glory like the stars; those who rejected the gospel and lived wickedly
steps.explain: 1 Corinthians 15:40–42 and D&C 76 describe these three degrees of glory.

steps.prompt: According to D&C 131:1–4, what is required to obtain the highest degree of the celestial kingdom?
options: Serving a full-time mission
Entering the new and everlasting covenant of marriage
Holding a leadership calling
Memorizing the scriptures
steps.explain: D&C 131:1–4 teaches that eternal marriage, sealed in the temple and kept faithfully, is required for the highest degree of celestial glory.

steps.prompt: Put the stages of the plan of salvation in order.
steps.hint: Follow a life from before birth to after death. Judgment comes after the body is raised again.
items: Premortal life
Birth and mortal life
Death and the spirit world
Resurrection
Final judgment
Kingdoms of glory
steps.explain: Being able to draw this sequence on paper is one of the simplest and most effective ways to teach Lesson 2.

steps.prompt: A friend asks: “So do you think everyone who isn’t a member of your church goes to hell?” What is the best answer?

options.text: “No. We believe God loves all His children. Almost everyone will receive a kingdom of glory, and people who never heard the gospel will have the chance to accept it after death. The gospel helps us receive the fullest joy God offers.”
options.feedback: Accurate and warm. It reflects D&C 76, D&C 138 and God’s love for all.

options.text: “Yes, only members are saved.”
options.feedback: This is not what the Church teaches.

options.text: “Everyone ends up in the same place, so it doesn’t matter.”
options.feedback: Also inaccurate. Choices and covenants matter.

options.text: “I don’t want to talk about that.”
options.feedback: A great teaching moment is lost. This doctrine often surprises and comforts people.

steps.explain: The restored doctrine of degrees of glory shows both God’s mercy and the importance of choices and covenants.

steps.title: Key takeaways
steps.body:
- Everyone will be resurrected with a perfect body of flesh and bones.
- Jesus Christ will judge us by our works and desires, with mercy for those who repent.
- There are three kingdoms of glory; the celestial is the fullest.
- Practise drawing the plan of salvation on a single sheet of paper.

units.title: The Gospel and Lifelong Discipleship
units.description: Lessons 3 and 4: the gospel of Jesus Christ, covenants, commandments and ordinances.

levels.title: Faith and Repentance
levels.summary: How faith grows and what real repentance looks like.

steps.title: Faith grows by testing it
steps.body:
Faith in Jesus Christ is “the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen” (Hebrews 11:1).

Moroni adds: “ye receive no witness until after the trial of your faith” (Ether 12:6). In other words, we act first, then the witness comes.

Alma compares this to planting a seed and watching whether it grows (Alma 32:27–43). Invitations give people a seed to plant.
steps.tip: Before you invite anyone to act in faith, do the same invitation yourself first, like reading a chapter and praying about it. Then you can share what happened.

source.label: PMG Lesson 3: Faith in Jesus Christ

steps.prompt: What does Ether 12:6 teach about how we gain a witness?
options: God gives a witness before we act so we know what to do
We receive a witness after we exercise faith
A witness only comes to prophets
We should wait for a sign before trying
steps.explain: “Ye receive no witness until after the trial of your faith.” Acting in faith comes first.

steps.title: Repentance: turning toward God
steps.body:
Repentance is not self-punishment. It is a change of mind, heart and behaviour that brings us closer to God, made possible by Jesus Christ. It includes:
- recognizing the sin and feeling godly sorrow
- confessing to God (and very serious sins to an authorized Church leader, such as your bishop)
- forsaking the sin and making things right where possible
- keeping the commandments

“He who has repented of his sins, the same is forgiven, and I, the Lord, remember them no more” (D&C 58:42).
steps.tip: End each day with a prayer reviewing what went well and what to do better. If something serious weighs on you, ask your bishop for a time to talk.

steps.prompt: Which are part of true repentance? Select all that apply.
options: Confessing and forsaking the sin
Godly sorrow for what you did
Making restitution where possible
Hiding the sin from God
Punishing yourself until you feel bad enough
steps.explain: D&C 58:43: “he will confess them and forsake them.” The Savior already paid for sin; we don’t earn forgiveness by suffering more.

steps.prompt: Repentance is mainly for people who have committed serious sins.
steps.explain: Everyone sins (Romans 3:23). Daily repentance is how all of us grow closer to Christ. Prophets have taught that repentance is a joyful, daily process.

steps.prompt: Match each scripture to its teaching on faith and repentance.
pairs: Faith is not a perfect knowledge of things
Christ can make weak things become strong
Sins as scarlet can become white as snow
Put off the natural man through the Atonement of Christ
The Lord forgives and remembers repented sins no more
steps.explain: Most of these are Doctrinal Mastery passages. They give hope: no one is beyond the Savior’s help.

steps.prompt: Lucas wants to be baptized but says: “I’ve tried to quit smoking ten times. I can’t do it.” What is the best response?

options.text: Show compassion, share Ether 12:27, make a specific plan together with daily contact, involve a supportive member, and tell him about the Church’s addiction recovery support.
options.feedback: This combines hope in Christ with practical help, as PMG chapter 10 recommends for addictions.

options.text: Tell him to come back when he has quit.
options.feedback: This abandons him when he most needs support.

options.text: Set a baptism date anyway and hope it works out.
options.feedback: Keeping the Word of Wisdom is required for baptism; skipping the issue doesn’t help him.

options.text: Tell him he just needs more willpower.
options.feedback: Addiction often needs more than willpower. Point him to the Savior and real support.

steps.explain: Repentance and change are possible through Jesus Christ, and missionaries walk with people through it with love, plans and member support.

steps.prompt: Daily repentance is a missionary habit. What is one thing you want to change with the Savior’s help this week, and what is your first small step?
steps.placeholder: I want to... My first step is...

levels.title: Baptism and the Holy Ghost
levels.summary: The baptismal covenant, the gift of the Holy Ghost and enduring to the end.

steps.title: Baptism: our first covenant
steps.body:
Jesus was baptized by immersion (Matthew 3:16) and taught that we must be “born of water and of the Spirit” (John 3:5). Baptism:
- is by immersion, by someone holding priesthood authority
- brings remission of sins and membership in the Church
- symbolizes the death of the old life and a new birth (Romans 6:3–5)

In the covenant we promise to be willing to take upon us Christ’s name, keep His commandments, serve God and others, and endure to the end. God promises forgiveness and His Spirit (Mosiah 18:8–10).
steps.tip: Read Mosiah 18:8–10 and write two lists: what we promise in the baptismal covenant and what God promises. Keep it with your scriptures.

steps.prompt: Which are part of the baptismal covenant we make? Select all that apply.
options: Be willing to take upon us the name of Jesus Christ
Keep God’s commandments
Serve God and others, bearing one another’s burdens
Never make another mistake
Endure to the end
steps.explain: We promise to keep trying, not to be perfect. When we fall short, we repent and renew our covenants through the sacrament.

steps.prompt: Children are baptized at age 8 because that is when they become accountable; little children do not need baptism.
steps.explain: D&C 68:25–27 sets age eight, and Moroni 8 teaches that little children are alive in Christ and need no baptism.

steps.title: The gift of the Holy Ghost
steps.body:
After baptism, a person is confirmed and receives the gift of the Holy Ghost by the laying on of hands by Melchizedek Priesthood holders (Articles of Faith 1:4; Acts 8:14–17).

Anyone can feel the **influence** of the Holy Ghost, which is how people gain a testimony (Moroni 10:5). The **gift** is the right to His constant companionship as we stay worthy. He comforts, guides, warns and sanctifies (3 Nephi 27:20).

source.label: PMG Lesson 3: The Gift of the Holy Ghost

steps.prompt: What is the difference between feeling the influence of the Holy Ghost and having the gift of the Holy Ghost?
steps.hint: Think about how people who are not yet members can gain a testimony, and what changes after confirmation.
options: There is no difference
The influence can come to anyone seeking truth; the gift is the right to His constant companionship after confirmation
The gift is only for missionaries
The influence comes only after baptism
steps.explain: People feel the Spirit before baptism (that is how they gain a testimony). The gift, given at confirmation, offers His constant companionship as they keep covenants.

steps.title: Enduring with the sacrament
steps.body:
Jesus gave the sacrament “in remembrance of me” (Luke 22:19–20). Each week, members renew their covenants and promise to always remember Him, and He promises that His Spirit will be with them (Moroni 4–5).

This is how enduring to the end really works: weekly renewal, daily repentance, steady progress toward the temple.
steps.tip: Read the sacrament prayers in Moroni 4 and 5 before church this Sunday, then listen closely to the words during the meeting.

steps.prompt: Put these steps of someone joining the Church in order.
steps.hint: An interview comes before the ordinance, and confirmation comes after baptism.
items: Learns the gospel and feels the Spirit
Repents and decides to follow Jesus Christ
Has a baptismal interview
Is baptized by immersion
Is confirmed and receives the gift of the Holy Ghost
Takes the sacrament weekly and prepares for the temple
steps.explain: Conversion continues after baptism. Lesson 4 is designed for this ongoing discipleship.

steps.prompt: A recent convert, Grace, tells you: “I lost my temper and swore at my brother. I think I ruined my baptism.” What do you say?

options.text: Reassure her that the covenant path includes repentance. Invite her to repent, apologize to her brother, and take the sacrament this Sunday to renew her covenants. Share how the Savior helps you too.
options.feedback: Accurate, hopeful and practical. The sacrament is the Lord’s provision for exactly this.

options.text: “That’s serious. You may need to be baptized again.”
options.feedback: Baptism is not repeated for sins. Repentance and the sacrament renew the covenant.

options.text: “Don’t worry about it, it’s not a big deal.”
options.feedback: Dismissive. She has a sincere desire to do better; help her repent.

options.text: Tell her to talk to the bishop right away before taking the sacrament.
options.feedback: Bishops help with serious sins; everyday mistakes are repented of directly with the Lord.

steps.explain: The sacrament lets members renew their baptismal covenants each week. Enduring to the end means continuing to repent and press forward.

steps.title: Key takeaways
steps.body:
- Baptism is by immersion, by priesthood authority, and is our first covenant.
- The covenant: take Christ’s name, keep commandments, serve, endure.
- The gift of the Holy Ghost is given by the laying on of hands.
- The sacrament renews our covenants each week.

levels.title: Commandments and Ordinances
levels.summary: Lesson 4: covenants, key commandments and the ordinances of salvation.

steps.title: Lesson 4 is built on covenants
steps.body:
Lesson 4 is organized around the baptismal covenant:
- **Take Christ’s name:** pray often, study the scriptures.
- **Keep the commandments:** the two great commandments, follow the prophet, the Ten Commandments, the law of chastity, tithing, the Word of Wisdom, the Sabbath, obey the law.
- **Serve God and others:** service, sharing the gospel, fasting and fast offerings.
- **Endure to the end:** priesthood, family, temple and family history.

Commandments are blessings: those who keep them are “blessed in all things” (Mosiah 2:41).
steps.tip: Pick one commandment from Lesson 4 that you find hardest and make one specific plan for it this week. Talk with a parent or leader if you want help.

steps.prompt: Match each commandment to a key scripture for it.
steps.hint: Isaiah 58 appears twice. One part is about the Lord's day, the other about loosing bands and feeding the hungry.
steps.explain: These are the core scriptures Preach My Gospel and Doctrinal Mastery use for each commandment.

steps.title: Explaining key commandments simply
steps.body:
- **Law of chastity:** sexual relations only between a man and a woman who are legally married.
- **Word of Wisdom:** no alcohol, tobacco, coffee, tea, or other harmful, illegal or addictive substances; care for your body (D&C 89).
- **Tithing:** give one-tenth of your income to the Lord (D&C 119:4). It funds the Lord’s work, such as temples and meetinghouses; local leaders are not paid.
- **Sabbath:** worship, take the sacrament, rest and do good on the Lord’s day.

Always connect a commandment to the promised blessing.

steps.prompt: Which is the most accurate way to explain tithing?
options: Giving 10% of your income to the Lord through His Church, with a promise of blessings (Malachi 3:10)
A monthly membership fee to belong to the Church
Giving whatever you feel is fair, any time
Paying the bishop’s salary
steps.explain: Tithing is one-tenth of income, given voluntarily as an act of faith. It is not a fee, and local leaders in the Church are unpaid.

steps.title: Ordinances of salvation and exaltation
steps.body:
An **ordinance** is a sacred act performed by priesthood authority, usually with a covenant. “In the ordinances thereof, the power of godliness is manifest” (D&C 84:20).

The ordinances of salvation and exaltation are:
- baptism
- confirmation and the gift of the Holy Ghost
- conferral of the Melchizedek Priesthood (for men)
- the temple endowment
- the temple sealing (eternal marriage)

The sacrament renews these covenants each week.
steps.tip: If you do not have a temple recommend, talk with your bishop about what you need to do. Then plan regular temple trips with your family or ward.

steps.prompt: Which of these are ordinances of salvation and exaltation? Select all that apply.
options: Baptism
Temple endowment
Patriarchal blessing
Temple sealing
Confirmation
Naming and blessing a baby
steps.explain: Patriarchal blessings and baby blessings are sacred ordinances, but they are not required for exaltation. The required ones are baptism, confirmation, Melchizedek Priesthood ordination (for men), endowment and sealing.

steps.prompt: Lesson 4 teaches that keeping enough commandments earns salvation on our own, without needing Jesus Christ.
steps.explain: We are saved by the grace and Atonement of Jesus Christ. Keeping commandments and covenants is how we follow Him and receive His power, not how we earn salvation alone (2 Nephi 25:23).

steps.prompt: Sofia says: “Tithing sounds like the Church just wants my money.” What is the best response?

options.text: Thank her for being honest. Explain that tithing is an ancient law (Malachi 3:8–10), that it funds the Lord’s work while local leaders are unpaid, share a personal experience of blessings, and invite her to pray about it.
options.feedback: Respectful, factual, personal, and it leaves the choice with her.

options.text: Tell her she can’t be baptized unless she agrees right now.
options.feedback: Pressure is not how missionaries teach. Help her understand and gain her own witness first.

options.text: Say tithing is optional, so she doesn’t need to worry.
options.feedback: Tithing is a commandment. Being inaccurate to avoid discomfort breaks trust later.

options.text: Skip tithing and come back to it after baptism.
options.feedback: People should understand the commitments of baptism before they are baptized.

steps.explain: Address concerns kindly and honestly, teach the doctrine and its blessings, and invite people to act in faith.

steps.prompt: Pick one commandment from Lesson 4 that you want to live more fully before your mission. How will you live it this month, and what blessing are you hoping for?
